source:
A pilot survey conducted by the fictional Eastborough Transit Group examined passengers' experiences of a revised bus timetable. Researchers invited 120 passengers to take part, and 72 completed the questionnaire. Of those respondents, 46 reported that the new departure times made their usual journey more convenient. These responses describe perceived convenience and do not establish that buses arrived more reliably.

Several respondents welcomed the earlier morning departure, while others said the longer interval between evening services made connections more difficult. The questionnaire did not collect information about journeys that passengers had stopped making. It therefore cannot show how the revised timetable affected people who chose another form of transport.

The group plans to keep the timetable unchanged for a further four weeks while collecting separate records of arrival times. Participation in another questionnaire would remain optional. No decision has been made about retaining the timetable permanently.

The results may help identify issues for further investigation, but they should not be treated as representative of every passenger. People who completed the questionnaire may have had different experiences from those who did not respond. A broader assessment would need to consider operational records as well as passenger feedback.
